key_insight: R-DMesh introduces a rectified dynamic mesh flow that separates pose alignment from temporal motion modeling, allowing a static 3D mesh to be robustly animated by a reference video even when initial poses mismatch. This rectification prevents severe geometric distortion and animation failure caused by naïve tracking.
problem_solved: Solves the pose misalignment dilemma: aligning a user-provided static mesh with the starting frame of a reference video so the mesh can follow the video-driven motion without distortion or failure.
method: Pose Rectification Module: estimates an alignment (rigid and local nonrigid) to bring the input mesh into correspondence with the video's initial frame.
Dynamic Mesh Flow Network: predicts per-vertex motion fields over time guided by video observations to drive temporally coherent deformations.
Regularization & Correspondence Refinement: geometric priors and video-based correspondences constrain deformations to preserve shape and avoid artifacts.
impact: Makes video-guided 3D animation practical and reliable for creators and ML pipelines by removing a common failure mode, lowering manual preprocessing, and improving automation for content creation, games, and AR/VR.
visual_elements: Before/After triptych: (1) original static mesh pose, (2) misaligned animation with distortion, (3) rectified R-DMesh animation result
Pipeline diagram showing: Pose Rectification -> Dynamic Mesh Flow -> Regularization & Output
Per-vertex flow visualization: color-coded motion vectors overlaid on mesh across frames
Failure-case comparison chart: qualitative examples where naive methods fail vs. R-DMesh succeeds
paper_title: R-DMesh: Video-Guided 3D Animation via Rectified Dynamic Mesh Flow
paper_authors: Zijie Wu, Lixin Xu, Puhua Jiang, Sicong Liu, Chunchao Guo
